- Launcher looks are listed Windows 11, 10, 7, Windows Phone, XP, 95, One UI, ColorOS, Terminal, then Material and AMOLED; Windows 11 is the look when none is saved (it was Material).
- Windows 11 colour settings: the accent variants are Light, Dark and Darker (no more 'pure'); the lit quick-settings tiles and sliders take the accent a notch darker.
- Launcher entry icon is the Windows 11 one (it was the old pulse line); the Windows 11 taskbar shows the Wi-Fi arcs when on Wi-Fi (the globe only without a connection).
- Windows desktop: windows snapping to a side edge is off by default (a setting turns it on); a window narrower than a phone shows its page scaled to fit (setting, on); the title bar press brings a window to the front; the Control Panel follows the Windows 11 look; search results of Settings each have their own icon.
- Terminal: the page is see-through black (the app's background shows through), not solid black.
- Game Hub CD shelf: a game with no picture yet shows a coloured cover with its name, so the shelf no longer sits on Loading.
- Code: inside a window of the desktop the editor opens in that window (not full screen); the row of language names is one language icon with a list; the menu of the three lines shows the folder tree (pick the folder, folders open and close, a file opens).
- Widgets: a nearly square widget gets a square frame; dragging the corner locks the size to another widget's size (each side) or to a square; the held widget has a button that gives every widget its size.
- Game Hub CD shelf: the covers are read small (360 px) four at a time, only the first 120 games are on the rack, the games with no cover are looked for in the background, and the rack is built again once when that search ends (not at every cover found).
